items.text: Social media has altered business, politics, and friendships, making going viral a household term. <break time="0.8s" /> The global financial industry links every bank and countless households in every country, making us vulnerable to human error taking place on the other side of the world. <break time="0.8s" /> As Columbia University strategy professor Rita McGrath explains, years ago most of our institutions were separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors outside their walls. <break time="0.8s" /> That is no longer the case. <break time="0.8s" /> The digitization of massive amounts of information has continued to grow enormously as the cost of computing power has decreased. <break time="0.8s" /> The development of smart systems that communicate autonomously gave rise to an infinite variety of potential breakdowns. <break time="0.8s" /> This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. <break time="0.8s" /> As Rita puts it, when things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what is going to happen next. <break time="0.8s" /> Information technology creates new vulnerabilities because interconnectedness instantly spreads the impact of small failures.
